key_source.description: Where the master key comes from: auto|prompt|systemd-cred|plainfile. Names a SOURCE, never key material, which is why GH #138 puts it on the params surface while the passphrase itself stays an environment variable this cell only NAMES (`params.unlock_env`). Set EXPLICITLY to systemd-cred or plainfile, the vault unlocks itself from that source at first use (GH #1058); auto keeps a woken vault locked.

key_file.description: The passphrase file read when key_source is plainfile (GH #1061, R-VG-7): an absolute path, mode 0600, holding only the passphrase. Settable through override_params, so a template instantiation (or scripts/start.sh) can point the vault at the file it unlocks from. A file PATH, not its content; for a long-running unit prefer key_source systemd-cred.

credential_name.description: The file read under $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY when key_source resolves to systemd-cred. A file NAME, not its content.

description.purpose: The vault cell: an encrypted store plus an executor. XChaCha20-Poly1305 per secret, argon2id from the passphrase, one operation that USES a secret (HMAC-SHA256) so the key does work and stays home -- the ssh-agent shape -- and one that DELIVERS it sealed to an ephemeral key the requester minted for that single call (GH #421). There is still no operation that returns a secret in the clear.
description.use_when: Interior cell of the access hive, and NOT one of its ports -- the generic boundary refuses any edge from outside the scope to it. `params.broker` is `./invoke`, the cell that validated the grant; and because nothing outside can address it, a DEPLOYMENT that wants this vault usable has to let it open itself: `params.key_source` set EXPLICITLY to `systemd-cred` (the passphrase as the systemd credential `$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY/<credential_name>`, `LoadCredentialEncrypted=` keeps it off the disk in the clear -- the path for a unit, GH #1058) or to `plainfile` with `key_file` (a 0600 file, the path without a unit), or `params.unlock_env` set to the environment variable holding its passphrase, which wins when both are set -- the key is DECLARED here as `null` so that a manifest can set it through `override_params`; a key that is not declared names no param, and the one setting every deployment has to make would have been the one setting no instantiation could make -- a vault in a sealed hive cannot be unlocked over the user channel, so it opens itself from its configured source or not at all (GH #427, GH #1058; `auto` never opens itself). The key ships UNSET on purpose: `a woken vault is locked` stays the default truth, and opening one is a decision an operator makes. The older `params.inject_map` push is gone (GH #428).
description.not_in_scope: There is no `get`, and adding one would not be a feature but a different cell type -- `deliver` is not one in disguise: what it returns is a ciphertext whose key exists in one requesting task's RAM and dies with it. A woken vault is always LOCKED -- the key lives in the task and dies with it, because a key that survives a sleep would have to be kept somewhere worse than the problem it solves.
